content: ZERIT® is the trade name for stavudine (d4T), which is a synthetic analogue of thymidine nucleoside. It exhibits antiviral activity specifically against human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1). The chemical designation of stavudine is 2′,3′-didehydro-3′-deoxythymidine. Stavudine appears as a white to off-white crystalline solid. Its molecular formula is C10H12N2O4, and it has a molecular weight of 224.2 g/mol. At a temperature of 23°C, stavudine demonstrates a solubility of approximately 83 mg/mL in water and 30 mg/mL in propylene glycol. The n-octanol/water partition coefficient of stavudine at 23°C is 0.144, indicating its relative hydrophilicity. ZERIT is available in two pharmaceutical forms: 1. Capsules for Oral Administration: The capsules are available in dosages of 15 mg, 20 mg, 30 mg, or 40 mg of stavudine. Each capsule contains the following inactive ingredients: microcrystalline cellulose, sodium starch glycolate, lactose, and magnesium stearate. The capsule shell is composed of gelatin, titanium dioxide, and iron oxides, and the capsules are printed with edible inks. 2. Powder for Oral Solution: ZERIT is also available as a dye-free, fruit-flavored powder. When reconstituted with water according to the instructions on the label, it provides a 1 mg/mL stavudine oral solution in a total volume of 200 mL. The powder formulation includes the following inactive ingredients: methylparaben, propylparaben, sodium carboxymethylcellulose, sucrose, and additional antifoaming and flavoring agents.
